title: AMD's Radeon RX 9070 GRE graphics card crashes to $529, below original MSRP
content: Grab a new 12GB GPU for less than the MSRP launch price.

title: Gigaphoton debuts neon recycling system with claimed 50% recovery rate
content: New neon gas recycling systems promise to reduce the demand for the noble gas at major chip manufacturers using DUV lithography. But as that technology is supplanted, this much-needed fix may only be needed temporarily.

title: EV charging company plans to deploy 100,000 Nvidia GPUs in pods at its roadside sites across the US
content: EV charging firm Xeal plans to use its existing U.S. network to deploy the 'world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity.'

title: Data center construction spending hits record $85 billion annual pace
content: Census Bureau data shows U.S. data center construction spending hit a record $85 billion annual rate in August, up 73% in a year.

title: Qualcomm will pay Huawei to license its patents for the first time in historic turnaround
content: Huawei and Qualcomm sign a multi-year patent cross-license covering 5G and AI, with Qualcomm buying some Huawei US patents.

title: OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design
content: OpenAI and Synopsys are developing GPT-Synopsys, a specialized semiconductor-design model that will directly operate Synopsys EDA tools

title: Used PS5 Pros now cost $1,399 at GameStop, 50% more than new ones
content: The price increase on refurbished PS5 Pros comes as the console remains out of stock at MSRP on various retailers, including directly from Sony. Best Buy and Walmart have new units in stock, but at around $1,500 each.

title: Elon Musk pledges SpaceXSI rebrand after Trump's executive order to use 'Super Intelligence' moniker
content: Elon Musk says he plans to rename SpaceXAI as SpaceXSI to reflect the new "Super Intelligence" moniker adopted in President Trump's executive order

title: Samsung 9100 Pro SSDs slashed up to 41% while supplies last — huge price cuts hit all capacities from 1TB to 8TB
content: Amazon slashes the prices of Samsung's entire 9100 Pro lineup of PCIe 5.0 SSDs during the Big Deals sale.

title: ADATA posts record 3Q revenue as memory prices rise
content: ADATA Technology reported record consolidated revenue of NT$53.03 billion(NT$53.03 billion)in the third quarter of 2026, topping NT$50 billion for the period as tighter memory supply and higher prices lifted sales. The memory module maker also said September consolidated revenue reached NT$15.73 billion, up 200% year-over-year but down 16.9% from August after it strategically adjusted shipments.

title: Cerebras' stock slide stops after Sam Altman calls it 'close partner'
content: Cerebras' stock rebounded by 9% after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman gave reassurance that the two companies are close partners days after a report cast doubt on their relationship, causing the chipmaker's stock to drop 20% last week. The episode raises concerns over its current concentration on a few large customers.

title: TSMC Texas-Terafab buzz drives Taiwan contractors to move fast
content: TSMC has not officially announced anything, but Taiwan's semiconductor facility engineering supply chain is already rushing to Texas after reports that the company is discussing a collaboration with Elon Musk's "Terafab" plan. DYC chairman Chung-Ping Hsieh said his company only received the news last week and has already begun mapping out a Texas strategy, while some faster-moving Taiwan contractors have even set up local offices.

title: LG lands 5GW North American data center cooling deal
content: LG Electronics has signed a long-term agreement to supply chillers for data center projects totaling more than 5GW of capacity in the US and Canada, giving the South Korean company greater visibility into future demand as it expands its North American cooling business.

title: BenQ Materials expands Xpore circular textile push
content: BenQ Materials showcased its eco-friendly performance fabric brand Xpore at the Taipei Innovative Textile Application Show (TITAS) 2026, marking the brand's second appearance at the event. The company introduced three core green technologies, six product lines and the commercial rollout of Xpore e2cycle, its electronic-waste recycling process, as it seeks a larger role in the global green materials supply chain.

title: AMD to expand Taiwan supply chain investment as AI demand drives capacity needs
content: AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company plans to further increase investment in Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain as demand for CPUs, GPUs, and AI computing continues to outpace available capacity.

title: ITRI sees hardware, AI, sensing drive quadruped robot rollout
content: As AI advances rapidly, the robotics industry is evolving from traditional automation equipment into a productivity tool for every industry, Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) said. ITRI added that robots will gradually move into manufacturing, inspection, welding, warehousing, medical care, and even homes, and that hardware, AI, sensing, and virtual-physical integration will be key to turning robots from simply machines that can move into ones that can work.

title: Chinese LCD panel makers tighten supply to lift prices — Taiwan suppliers eye order shifts
content: Chinese panel makers moved to cut production during the National Day holiday after issuing their first price increase notices in September, combining pricing signals with supply controls to stabilize LCD TV panel prices and profitability.

title: China's 15th five-year plan elevates PCB role in AI supply chains
content: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the National Development and Reform Commission have released the 15th Five-Year Plan for the development of the electronic information manufacturing industry, aiming to push revenue at large-scale enterprises above CNY30 trillion (US$4.5 trillion) by 2030 and foster world-class companies in semiconductors, advanced computing, consumer electronics, basic electronics, and energy electronics.

title: Samsung secures customer backing for US$5B substrate expansion
content: Samsung Electro-Mechanics is investing KRW6.78 trillion (approx. US$5 billion) to expand FCBGA capacity in South Korea and Vietnam. The projects are backed by customer funding and medium- to long-term volume commitments, as demand for high-performance package substrates pushes Korean production lines toward high utilization.

title: Taiwan bets on SiPh, CPO to tackle AI data center power bottlenecks
content: Taiwan's National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) has launched two research programs targeting silicon photonics (SiPh) and next-generation AI data center power systems, seeking to address energy and performance bottlenecks as high-speed computing shifts increasingly from copper to optical interconnects.

title: TSMC tops global FDI ranking as AI infrastructure redraws overseas investment
content: The direction of global corporate investment in physical assets is becoming clearer. According to the fDi Report 2026 and an analysis by Visual Capitalist, announced greenfield foreign direct investment by multinational companies exceeded US$1.3 trillion in 2025, up 2.2% from a year earlier.

title: Taiwan's NSTC seeks AI data center power tech to reduce grid impact of load spikes
content: Taiwan's National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) has recently issued a call for proposals on "high-performance power conversion and system management technologies for next-generation AI data centers." The aim is to help AI-related industries discover and develop usable technologies that can reduce AI's impact on the power grid. The effort targets power consumption, the single biggest customer-side issue facing companies in AI chip design and manufacturing and AI server assembly.

title: Apple, Qualcomm renew patent deal, iPhone modem shift deepens
content: Qualcomm announced on September 24 that it has renewed its global patent licensing agreement with Apple, with the new contract set to take effect on April 1, 2027. The terms and value of the deal were not disclosed, but Apple's long-running move toward in-house modem chips continues to draw close attention.

title: Drone share tops 10% as Calin Technology eyes LEO optics, auto growth
content: Optical lens maker Calin Technology is seeing its new business ventures bear fruit. Revenue from its drone camera module segment has surpassed 10% of total sales in 2026 and is targeting over 15%, making it the company's fastest-growing product line this year. Meanwhile, automotive lens revenue is projected to remain flat in 2026 before returning to growth in 2027, driven by a new design-in project with a US automaker.

title: Nittobo expands glass cloth output as AI chip demand strains global supply
content: Nittobo is expanding production of its T-Glass glass cloth as demand from AI chip makers tightens a critical part of the global semiconductor supply chain. The move matters beyond Japan because shortages of this insulating material could slow advanced chip production, raise costs, and affect technology markets worldwide.

title: How RobCo and the robotics unicorn wave are redefining industrial automation
content: Physical AI is shifting from a hardware niche into the next foundational computing platform, driving record investor capital into embodied intelligence systems.

title: Arcadyan September revenue hits record on mobile communications strength
content: As the networking market enters its traditional peak season, customer demand is gradually recovering. Arcadyan Technology announced on October 5 its September revenue, which reached NT$5.06 billion (approx. US$159.3 million), up 7.0% month-over-month and 8.5% year-over-year. This marked a record high.
